newsitem.title: GERMANY: DIHT downbeat on German growth, investment.
newsitem.headline: DIHT downbeat on German growth, investment.

text.p: A leading German corporate lobby group said on Thursday that the economy was stagnating in the current quarter compared to the fourth quarter of 1996, and it expected growth of two percent for this year as a whole.
The Federation of German Chambers of Industry and Commerce (DIHT) said that its new-year survey of companies' plans showed that they were still not prepared to boost investment.
"Our survey results indicate that the German economy did not grow during the first quarter," DIHT spokesman Franz Schoser told reporters.
He added: "We have the impression that at the beginning of the year the readiness to invest was not there."

The German government is standing by its forecast of 2.5 percent growth this year, despite a further climb in unemployment to a post-war record of nearly 4.7 million in February. The growth forecast underpins plans to cut borrowing this year in order to qualify for European monetary union.
In a statement released earlier, the DIHT said that the economic recovery was struggling to make progress, but there were bright spots in the economic landscape.
Exports will continue to drive the economy in 1997, thanks to global economic recovery and the depreciation of the German mark.

But domestic growth remains weak, with investment and consumer demand slowing development and "gloomy" prospects for the building sector. Employment by companies will be lower this year than last, with many more planning to downsize rather than those intending hire fresh staff.

The DIHT added that the hopes of companies depended on a growth-friendly tax reform -- which is currently being discussed by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition and the opposition Social Democrats (SPD).
